edges.description: BCG vaccination introduces the live attenuated mycobacterium that then replicates unchecked in macrophages that cannot be activated without IFN-gamma.

nodes.description: Routine BCG immunisation is the sentinel environmental exposure in this disorder. The attenuated Mycobacterium bovis BCG strain is harmless to immunocompetent infants but disseminates in patients who cannot mount IFN-gamma-dependent macrophage activation, which is how MSMD patients typically come to attention.

evidence.reference_title: Inherited human IFN-γ deficiency underlies mycobacterial disease.
evidence.snippet: Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease (MSMD) is characterized by a selective predisposition to clinical disease caused by the Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine and environmental mycobacteria.

nodes.description: The homozygous IFNG frameshift allele is a loss-of-expression, loss-of-function allele, so no functional interferon gamma is made. This is the initiating lesion: every downstream step follows from the absence of the cytokine, not from any defect in its receptor or in downstream signal transduction.

evidence.reference_title: Inherited human IFN-γ deficiency underlies mycobacterial disease.
evidence.snippet: The mutant allele is loss of expression and loss of function.

nodes.description: IFN-gamma is the principal macrophage-activating cytokine. Without it, the IFN-gamma receptor on mononuclear phagocytes is never engaged, the JAK1/JAK2-STAT1 cascade is not triggered, and the antimicrobial programme that allows macrophages to restrict intracellular mycobacteria is not induced. The receptor and its signalling machinery are structurally intact here, which is what distinguishes this etiology from the IFN-gamma receptor deficiencies and makes it pharmacologically addressable with the recombinant cytokine.

evidence.reference_title: Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease: genetic, immunological, and clinical features of inborn errors of IFN-γ immunity.
evidence.snippet: The nine gene products are physiologically related, as all are involved in IFN-γ-dependent immunity.

nodes.description: T lymphocytes and natural killer cells are the physiological sources of IFN-gamma in the IL-12/IFN-gamma circuit. In these patients both compartments fail to produce or secrete detectable IFN-gamma, so the effector limb of the circuit is silent even though IL-12 production and IL-12 receptor signalling are intact.

evidence.snippet: The blood T and NK lymphocytes from these patients also failed to produce and secrete detectable amounts of IFN-γ.

nodes.description: The clinical phenotype. Disease ranges from localized BCG-itis at the vaccination site to disseminated BCG-osis and infection with environmental mycobacteria, and extends beyond mycobacteria: roughly half of MSMD patients also suffer clinical disease caused by non-typhoidal Salmonella, and milder chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis and other intramacrophagic infections are reported. One of the two reported IFN-gamma-deficient patients was diagnosed with BCG-osis after lymph node biopsy confirmed acid-fast bacilli.

evidence.reference_title: Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease: genetic, immunological, and clinical features of inborn errors of IFN-γ immunity.
evidence.snippet: MSMD designation does not recapitulate all the clinical features, as patients are also prone to salmonellosis, candidiasis and tuberculosis, and more rarely to infections with other intramacrophagic bacteria, fungi, or parasites, and even, perhaps, a few viruses.

nodes.description: Subcutaneous recombinant IFN-gamma is the mechanistically rational therapy for this specific MSMD etiology. Because the defect is in the cytokine and not in its receptor or in the downstream JAK-STAT1 machinery, exogenous IFN-gamma can engage an intact receptor and restore macrophage activation. This is the therapeutic distinction between IFNG deficiency and complete IFN-gamma receptor deficiency, in which the cytokine cannot act. Recombinant IFN-gamma has already proven useful in other MSMD etiologies with impaired IFN-gamma production, such as IL-12Rbeta1 deficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Inherited human IFN-γ deficiency underlies mycobacterial disease.
evidence.snippet: Human recombinant IFN-γ (IMUKIN) treatment (50 μg/m 2, 3 times per week) was started 18 months after the patient’s initial presentation.

nodes.description: Weakly virulent mycobacteria — BCG vaccine strains and environmental non-tuberculous mycobacteria — persist and replicate inside macrophages that cannot be activated. Containment fails at the level of the granuloma, permitting local and then disseminated infection with organisms that immunocompetent hosts control without clinical disease.

evidence.reference_title: Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease: genetic, immunological, and clinical features of inborn errors of IFN-γ immunity.
evidence.snippet: Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease (MSMD) is a rare condition characterized by predisposition to clinical disease caused by weakly virulent mycobacteria, such as BCG vaccines and environmental mycobacteria, in otherwise healthy individuals with no overt abnormalities in routine hematological and immunological tests.
